pte_elective_tax.rate_note: Colorado SALT Parity Act elective entity-level tax for partnerships and S corporations at the individual rate (4.4% for 2026). Not verified on a DOR page today.

personal_exemption.notes: Colorado starts from federal taxable income, so the federal standard deduction (or itemized deductions) is already subtracted; there is no separate Colorado standard deduction or exemption. Add-backs apply for high earners' deductions (state addback for itemized/standard deductions above certain AGI).

income_tax_2026.surtaxes: None. A temporary TABOR-triggered rate reduction (max 0.15 pt) is not expected for 2026 per the March 2026 Legislative Council forecast (search index).

estimated_tax.required_if: You expect to owe more than $1,000 in net Colorado tax for 2026 after withholding and credits
estimated_tax.notes: Required annual payment is the smaller of 70% of the current-year net liability or 100% of the prior year's (50% for farmers/fishers).

unemployment_2026.notes: 2026 non-construction introductory rate 3.05% (1.53% base + 0.17% support + 1.35% solvency surcharge); heavy construction 6.285%. For 2027 the wage base rises to $32,100 and the surcharge turns off (intro rate 1.70%). Colorado FAMLI paid leave premium 0.88% of wages for 2026, split 50/50 (per FAMLI pages, search index), also hits an S corp owner's salary.

local_taxes.name: Occupational Privilege Tax (OPT)
local_taxes.applies: Business OPT $4.00 per month for each owner, partner, manager (and each taxable employee) engaged in business in Denver, regardless of earnings; single-member disregarded LLC member taxed as an owner. Employee OPT $5.75 per month withheld from employees earning at least $500/month in Denver (S corp officer-employees fall here).
local_taxes.threshold_or_exemption: The $500 earnings test does not apply to owners or partners; any entity with activity in Denver owes at least $4.00 per month. Sole proprietors without employees may prepay the year by January 31.
local_taxes.quote: the employer is required to pay the Business OPT at a rate of $4.00 per month for each owner, partner, or manager engaged in business in Denver

notable: No LLC franchise tax and a $25 periodic report (raised from $10 in July 2024) (https://www.sos.state.co.us/pubs/info_center/fees/business.html)
Flat 4.4% on federal taxable income for 2026 (https://tax.colorado.gov/sites/default/files/documents/DR_0104EP_2026.pdf)

Denver charges a flat monthly head tax on owners: $48/year per owner even for a one-person LLC (https://www.denvergov.org/files/assets/public/v/2/finance/documents/treasury/tax-guides/taxguidetopic61_occupationalprivilegetaxes.pdf)
2026 new-employer UI rate includes a 1.35% solvency surcharge that ends in 2027 (https://cdle.colorado.gov/employers/unemployment-insurance-premiums/introductory-rates)
uncertain: PTET (SALT parity) availability and rate not read on an official page today.
Other Colorado occupational privilege taxes (Aurora, Greenwood Village, Sheridan, Glendale) not researched.
FAMLI 2026 rate (0.88%) from search index of famli.colorado.gov; a headcount notice suggests employers with nine or fewer employees pay only the 0.44% employee share.
